summary.text: Anab Mohamud is standing as an independent for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Wikipedia records that a Greens candidate of the same name won a seat on Yarra City Council in Langridge Ward in 2020 and left the Greens in 2024; no source we found confirms that this is the Essendon candidate. The ABC's guide lists the Essendon candidate without a biography as at 9 Nov 2026.

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia records a Yarra councillor of this name; no source we found says this is the 2026 Essendon candidate. The name isn't among Wikipedia's 2024 Yarra candidates, so the term has ended; no end year is given.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia records a Yarra councillor of this name; no source we found says this is the 2026 Essendon candidate.

summary.text: Ava Adams is a Moonee Valley City councillor running as an independent for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. She was elected to the council in 2020 and again in 2024, when she won Queens Park Ward, and was mayor for a year spanning 2024 and 2025. The ABC says her earlier work was in accounting, public relations and business consulting.

occupation.text: Councillor; previously worked in business consulting, public relations and accounting

summary.text: James Williams is the Greens candidate for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. A Wakka Wakka man originally from South East Queensland, he has made his home in Moonee Valley for almost two decades. Before becoming an emergency services officer, he was an ICT manager and computer engineer with a large not-for-profit organisation.

prior_roles.role: Member, Friends of Moonee Ponds Creek

priorities.text: Clean energy from solar and wind
Safer local cycling routes and better public transport
Better opportunities for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in health, education and work
Support for refugees and people facing disadvantage

sources.title: Essendon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
James Williams, Candidate for Essendon, Australian Greens

summary.text: John Barnes is One Nation's candidate for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. A former ruckman, he played 202 AFL games across two stints at Essendon and eight seasons at Geelong, and was in Essendon's 2000 premiership team. He has been the Buckley Ward councillor on Moonee Valley City Council since 2024; Wikipedia lists the Liberal Party as his former party.

occupation.text: Former AFL footballer; Moonee Valley City councillor

prior_roles.organisation: Doutta Stars Football Club (Essendon District Football League)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia describes him as an 'Independent Liberal' candidate at this election; council ballots carry no party names.

priorities.text: I will speak honestly, stand by my principles and put people before politics.
No lies. No spin. No excuses.
Firmer treatment of repeat offenders, with victims put first and money spent on prevention
Practical government action to bring down household living costs
Junior sport open to every child whatever their family can afford

sources.title: Essendon - VIC Election 2026, ABC News election guide

summary.text: Katerine (Kat) Theodosis is Labor's candidate for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election, in which the sitting Labor member, Danny Pearson, is retiring. She has been a Labor councillor on Merri-bek City Council for Westbreen Ward since 2024. Her parents migrated from Greece, and her party page says she went to Strathmore Secondary College and has always lived in Melbourne's north-west.

priorities.text: Government investment in schools, hospitals and local infrastructure

summary.text: Michal Kedem is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a community lawyer whose work involves helping clients challenge police and other government agencies, and she is a union activist. She says she was among the organisers of two strikes in the community sector over Gaza during the last two years.

priorities.text: We need more funding for healthcare, education including childcare, and housing
Opposes more spending on police, prisons, defence and deportations
Holding police to account, and opposing recent laws that widen powers to search and detain young people
Better pay and conditions for community sector workers
Support for Palestine

sources.title: Essendon - VIC Election 2026, ABC News election guide
Michal Kedem, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Oscar Yildiz is standing as an independent for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. A teacher by training, he was first elected to Moreland (now Merri-bek) City Council in 2008 and has been its mayor twice. He came second in Pascoe Vale at the 2018 state election, and he founded the anti-bullying charity Bully Zero Australia Foundation.

prior_roles.organisation: Merri-bek City Council (Moreland City Council until 2022)

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he was elected in 2008 but not under what label; council ballots carry no party names, so it is recorded as independent.
The ABC says he finished second with 41.4% of the two-candidate-preferred vote but doesn't state the label he ran under.

priorities.text: responsible planning that puts infrastructure before overdevelopment
My loyalty is to the people that live in the Seat of Essendon
Relief from living costs for households, and more help for pensioners, carers, veterans and people with disability
More police on local streets, and police stations at Moonee Ponds and Flemington open to the public again
An upgraded Essendon Station and a Route 59 tram line running on from Airport West to Melbourne Airport

summary.text: Tommy Le Deux is the Liberal candidate for Essendon at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he works in corporate finance at NAB and also has a part-time job at a hotel in Ascot Vale. He has run for Moonee Valley City Council in the past and was a member of the council's committee for young people.

previous_candidacies.election: Moonee Valley City Council (year not stated)
previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he stood for the council but gives neither the year nor the result; council ballots carry no party names, so his current party code is used.
